attempted_claim: Let X be an AM-space isomorphic to a complemented subspace of a C(K)-space for some compact Hausdorff K, with X nonseparable. Must X be linearly isomorphic to a C(K')-space for some compact Hausdorff K'?
decisive_failure: correctness: TARGET route: claimed YES to complemented AM => C(K) via stronger universal 'every AM is C(K)'. Step 1 is false: general AM-space is lattice-embeddable as sublattice of C(K), not C0(L); Schaefer II.7.4 and Aliprantis-Burkinshaw 4.29 are unital Kakutani only, and principal-ideal gluing does not yield C0(L). Directly contradicted by Benyamini 1977 M-space cited in 2025 survey as nonseparable AM not isomorphic to C(K). Hyperplane lemma itself is correct folklore but inapplicable to arbitrary AM. Hence target Question 5 remains unproved and stronger claim is false. originality: Nearest prior is de Hevia-Tradacete 2025 survey which records the exact target verbatim as open Question 5 in Sec 7.2 and states separable AM=>C(K) fails nonseparably via Benyamini [11]; Sec 6(3) already contains the same two-point-identification hyperplane-is-C(K) proof. Kakutani is classical. Stronger universal claim was already decided negatively by Benyamini 1977 publisher body (non-separable M-space not C(K)). No new boundary, object, or implication. value: No valid resolution is established: the proof is invalid and the stronger universal statement is known false, so there is no retrievable exact invariant, witness, or classification advance. Combination of textbook unital Kakutani plus folklore hyperplane fact with false C0(L) extension is a textbook restatement with erroneous generalization. Open Question 5 is unchanged; no independently useful downstream fact is created.
